RMediation builds on medfit's objects: it computes confidence intervals for a product of coefficients from the exact
distribution of the product (DOP) or Monte Carlo draws, and the model-based constrained-likelihood (MBCO) test for a
pair of fits. medfit supplies the fitting and extraction, its own delta-method intervals and `mbco_sem()`. This page
runs both on one fit and lists what RMediation accepts from medfit, with a status for each row that a test checks
against a live call on each build.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Use medfit when** | you want every effect and path from one object, a native `SEMFit`, or an interval from the bootstrap infrastructure |
| **Use RMediation when** | you want an interval from the distribution of a product (not a normal approximation), or `mbco()` on a restricted and a full `SEMFit` |
| **Both** | read the same `MediationData` and `SerialMediationData`; the `mbco()` p-value agrees with `mbco_sem()` on a product null |

The statements below were checked against RMediation 1.11.1 (a GitHub release) with medfit 0.16.0. RMediation is not
a dependency of medfit, so the chunks run only where RMediation 1.11.1 or later is installed; a site built without it
shows the code and the numbers quoted in the text. CRAN has 1.6.1, whose `mbco()` accepts only OpenMx models.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
ok <- requireNamespace("RMediation", quietly = TRUE) && utils::packageVersion("RMediation") >= "1.11.1"
```

## Three intervals for one indirect effect

```{r}
#| label: intervals
#| eval: !expr ok
fit <- fit_mediation(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1, mediator1 ~ treatment,
                     data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
dop <- RMediation::ci(fit, type = "dop")
mc <- RMediation::ci(fit, type = "MC", n.mc = 1e5)
delta <- suppressWarnings(confint(fit, parm = "effects"))["nie", ]
rbind(dop = dop$CI, monte_carlo = mc$CI, delta = unname(delta))
```

The indirect effect is 0.325. The exact-distribution interval is 0.172 to 0.488, the Monte Carlo interval agrees
to about 0.001, and medfit's delta-method interval is 0.168 to 0.483: symmetric around the estimate, where the
product's distribution is skewed. Which to report is in [Which interval should I use?](guide-intervals.html).

## MBCO from medfit and from RMediation

`mbco()` takes the restricted fit first. The product null `a * b = 0` is the union of `a = 0` and `b = 0`, and its
p-value is the larger of the two; medfit's `mbco_sem()` does that in one call.

```{r}
#| label: mbco
#| eval: !expr ok
model <- "mediator1 ~ a*treatment
outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment"
full <- fit_sem(model, mediation_demo)
null_a <- fit_sem(paste0(model, "\na == 0"), mediation_demo)
null_b <- fit_sem(paste0(model, "\nb == 0"), mediation_demo)
p_branch <- c(a = RMediation::mbco(null_a, full)$p_value, b = RMediation::mbco(null_b, full)$p_value)
c(rmediation_max = max(p_branch), medfit = mbco_sem(full, "a", "b")$p.value)
```

Both give 2.79e-05: the `a = 0` branch (chi-square 17.6 on 1 df) is the weaker one. RMediation's `mbco()` tests the one restriction that separates the two fits you give it, so the
product null takes two calls.

## Feature table

Status describes RMediation 1.11.1 acting on the medfit object in the first column.

| Feature | medfit | RMediation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interval for the NIE of a `MediationData` | `confint()`, `bootstrap_mediation()` | `ci()` | Supported |
| Interval for the NIE of a `SerialMediationData` | `confint()`, `bootstrap_mediation()` | `ci()` | Supported |
| Interval from a `ParallelMediationData` | `confint()`, `bootstrap_mediation()` | no method | Unsupported |
| Interval from an `InteractionMediationData` | `confint()`, `bootstrap_mediation()` | no method | Unsupported |
| Interval from a `SEMFit` directly | `tidy()`, `confint()` | no method | Unsupported |
| Interval from a `SEMFit` after `extract_mediation()` | `extract_mediation(<SEMFit>)` | `ci()` | Supported |
| MBCO for a restricted and a full `SEMFit` | `mbco_sem()` | `mbco()` | Supported |
| Quantile of a product of two normals | none | `qprodnormal()` | Supported |

"Unsupported" means the call fails today with a message that names the missing method, not that it never will;
check RMediation's own `NEWS.md` before relying on a row. medfit's `ClusterMediationData`,
`TwoLevelMediationData`, `JointMediationData` and the FIML classes are not in the table: they were not exercised here.

## What RMediation adds, and what it does not

- **Adds:** intervals from the distribution of a product (`ci(type = "dop")` and the Monte Carlo variant `type = "MC"`),
  the product-normal distribution functions (`pprodnormal()`, `qprodnormal()`), and `mbco()` for two fits.
- **Does not add:** fitting, extraction, effects beyond the product of coefficients, or a model class. It reads the
  properties of `MediationData`, `SerialMediationData` and `SEMFit` that medfit's `test-dependents-contract.R` pins.
